intro: Paraguay is a landlocked country in the heart of South America where an Indigenous language, Guaraní, is spoken by most people.

chapters.title: Guaraní and the Jesuit missions
text: The Guaraní people lived here when Spain founded Asunción in 1537. Jesuit priests built missions where Guaraní communities lived and worked; the ruins at Trinidad and Jesús are World Heritage sites.

chapters.title: Independence and the Great War
text: Paraguay became independent in 1811. From 1864 to 1870 it fought Brazil, Argentina and Uruguay in the War of the Triple Alliance, which killed a huge share of its population, perhaps half or more.

highlight.title: Devastation
highlight.text: Few modern wars have killed such a large share of a country's people.

chapters.title: Chaco and Stroessner
text: Paraguay won the Chaco War against Bolivia in 1935. Alfredo Stroessner ruled as dictator from 1954 to 1989. Democracy has continued since.
